headings.title: Employment efforts, wage trust accounts, garnishment, and taxes

Directs sheriffs or city wardens to seek work for unemployed prisoners, collect wages into a ledgered trust checking account, exempts wages from garnishment during the term, and treats them as prisoner income for tax purposes.

headings.title: Prisoner board liability, lunches, and self-employed forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Holds gainfully employed prisoners liable for board, requires carry-out lunches on request if absent at mealtime, authorizes charging accounts, and triggers automatic forfeiture of leave privileges if a self-employed prisoner defaults on board payment.

headings.title: Court-ordered disbursement of employed prisoners' wages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note. Lists the five purposes for sheriff disbursement of wages by sentencing court order: board, work travel and incidentals, dependent support, written or judgment obligations, and discharge balance.

headings.title: Intercounty employment arrangements between sheriffs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Permits court orders authorizing the committing sheriff to arrange with another county's sheriff for prisoner employment in that county while remaining subject to the commitment.

headings.title: Delegating sheriff or warden duties to welfare or clerk
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Permits transferring subsection 3 and/or 5 duties to a county or city welfare office by governing-body resolution upon sheriff/warden request, or otherwise to the sentencing court clerk by court order, effective until rescinded.

headings.title: Welfare office investigation of dependent support needs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Requires the county welfare office, at the sentencing court's request, to investigate and report the amount needed to support the prisoner's dependents.

headings.title: Sheriff suspension of leave privilege for violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Grants sheriffs permissive authority to withhold leave privileges for up to five consecutive days for breaches of discipline or violations of jail regulations.

headings.title: Three-fourths good-conduct discharge rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Entitles prisoners granted privileges under this section who serve three-fourths of their sentence in an orderly and peaceable manner to full discharge.

headings.title: Court sanctions for law or jail regulation violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Requires returning a prisoner who violates law or jail regulations to the sentencing court, which may order actual confinement for the remaining sentence and cancel earned term diminution.

headings.title: County suspension of section when facilities are unavailable
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Permits any county to suspend operation of section 221.170 by resolution or ordinance when proper facilities are unavailable.

headings.title: Prisoner employment authority in all other counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note. Authorizes county commissions of all other counties to prescribe rules and terms for employing state-statute jail prisoners (including fine nonpayment commitments) and applies earnings to judgments against them.
